turns.answer:
I've read the Loudon Live entry, its launch kit, the channel's design rules, LDN RTM and the Quality Manifesto. The draft is below. The Concierge couldn't be summoned first: a hook blocks agent spawns in this session. So I did the reading myself, and I haven't written to any file.

**The tension, said once.** Your own pages argue against this. The Quality Manifesto lists "optimized thumbnail/title (clickbait that works)" and "hooks in first 3 seconds" as *their* paradigm (`Quality Manifesto.md:137-141`). The design system's rules include "no hype" and no outcome promises in titles. It's your channel, so I followed the ask. I held one line: the copy promises nothing the videos won't deliver. As it turns out, the honest moves are also the ones that get clicks. Swap vague wording for specific nouns, open with real questions, and make RTM's thoroughness obvious.

**What I took "the pitch" to be:** sections 1–3 of `Projects/Loudon Live/Loudon Live — launch kit.md` (tagline, About, trailer). It's out of date. It's from May, it pitches only streams, and it says "Loudon Live." Since 2026-10-14 the entry has defined Loud'n Live as your teaching and coaching face, with RTM and coaching in it. The rewrite brings it up to date.

---

**Tagline**

> Every knob tested. Every build out loud.

**About** (the first line is what search and channel previews show)

> Loud'n Live is where I read the manual all the way through, test every claim in it, and build instruments and effects from scratch — on camera, for electronic musicians.
>
> **LDN RTM** takes one product's complete manual — Ableton Live 12 first — and gives every section its own short video, numbered to the manual so you can jump straight to the one you need. Compressor, Vocoder, Wavetable, all of it. Every parameter named, demonstrated, and given an honest opinion about what it's actually for. Sections land in complete chunks: all of Drift at once, never half a device.
>
> The livestreams push one project forward at a time — a synth from an empty patch, an effect from first principles, the question of why a sound feels warm. Sometimes it works first try. Usually the wall is where the good part is.
>
> I've taught music for twenty years, and I coach one-on-one: [link].
>
> New videos land without a schedule. Subscribe to get them when they do.

**Short version** (bios, panels)

> Every knob tested, every build out loud. Whole manuals, one short video per section — plus synths and effects built live.

**Trailer** (~50 sec, with no "Hi, I'm Loudon" opener; it starts on the content, the way RTM videos do)

> *[Cold open: hands on Live's Compressor, attack knob turning, the drum audibly changing]*
>
> This is the attack knob on Ableton's Compressor. The manual gives it one sentence. It deserves a video — so it gets one. So does every other section of the manual.
>
> I'm Loudon. This is Loud'n Live.
>
> I read manuals all the way through and test what they claim. It's how I learned every tool I know, and it's the fastest way I've found to stop guessing. Every section gets its own short video, numbered to the manual, so you can find the one you need at one in the morning and get back to your track.
>
> The other half is building — synths, effects, instruments, from an empty patch, live. One project at a time. Usually the wall is where the good part is.
>
> Twenty years teaching music. Come find out what your sounds are actually doing.

---

**Three changes that break rules you wrote down.** Each is yours to accept or refuse:

- **I cut the trailer's work-in-progress line.** Your direction was to name it once, in the trailer. It lowers conversion, and "the wall is where the good part is" keeps some of that honesty. Put it back if you want it.
- **RTM titles would get more clicks with the search term first.** People search "Live 12 Compressor," not "LDN RTM." So: `Live 12 Compressor — every parameter tested · LDN RTM 28.14`. That changes the address format the LDN RTM entry treats as fixed, so it's a decision for the house, not just a copy edit. Stream titles can lead with the question too (`Why does a sound feel warm? · Sound lab`), and that stays within the rules.
- **You can't tune for clicks you never look at.** RTM's rule is "no analytics, ever" (`Projects/LDN RTM.md:93`). If "maximize views" is a real shift and not a one-off, that rule is what it runs into.

Please check "twenty years." I took it from `Quality Manifesto.md:203`; the old kit only says "a long time." Also, the About describes RTM videos that haven't been recorded yet, since the pilot chunk is still ahead, so it should go up when they do.

**Where should this land?** I can replace sections 1–3 of the launch kit if you say "grow up," or it can wait for a session where the Concierge can be summoned to place it.
